Description: Set up development infrastructure including certificate management, Prometheus monitoring, and plugin navigation integration. This epic covers all foundational work needed before UI development can begin.

As a DevOps engineer, I want to generate all required PKI certificates for broker communication, so that BrokerServices and BrokerApps can communicate securely.

*Acceptance Criteria:*
- Certificate generation script exists and is documented
- Control Plane PKI certificates are generated (broker-cert, operator-manager-ca)
- Data Plane PKI certificates are generated (data-plane-broker-cert, data-plane-ca)
- App certificates are generated per application
- All certificates are stored as Kubernetes Secrets
- Script usage is documented in README

*What:* Script to generate all PKI certificates needed for broker communication

*Why:* Operator doesn't handle cert-manager yet, so we need a workaround

*Deliverables:*
- Script file with inline comments
- README section explaining usage
- Example invocation in docs
- Test: Run script and verify all secrets are created
- Test: Verify certificates have correct fields (CN, SAN, etc.)
- Test: Use generated certificates to connect broker and app

Provide UI for cluster administrators to create, list, and view BrokerService resources. BrokerServices represent messaging infrastructure (clusters, storage, PKI) managed by operators.

As a cluster administrator, I want to create a BrokerService with basic configuration, so that messaging infrastructure is available for applications.

*Acceptance Criteria:*
- Navigate to Workloads > Brokers in Administrator perspective
- Click "Create BrokerService"
- Fill in form: Name, Namespace (read-only), Labels (key-value pairs), Memory
- Switch between Form View and YAML View
- Submit form and verify BrokerService is created
- Verify StatefulSet, Services, and Secrets are created by operator

*Wireframe:* wireframe-service-creation.html

*What:* Form to create a BrokerService

*Features:*
- Form View / YAML View toggle (radio buttons)
- Name input with DNS-1123 validation
- Namespace display (read-only from project selector)
- Labels input: Simple key-value text fields (no ConfigMaps, no localStorage, no drag-and-drop)
- Memory input with unit dropdown (Mi/Gi)
- YAML editor with syntax highlighting
- Create button submits to K8s API
- Cancel button goes back

*Acceptance Criteria:*
- Can create BrokerService via form view
- Can create BrokerService via YAML view
- Form validates required fields (name, memory)
- Labels add/remove works correctly
- Resource appears in kubectl get brokerservices
- Error messages display if creation fails
- Test: Create service with valid inputs → verify success
- Test: Submit form with missing required fields → verify validation errors
- Test: Create service via YAML → verify it matches form-created resource
- Test: Add/remove multiple labels → verify they persist correctly

Display performance metrics for BrokerServices and BrokerApps using Prometheus queries and charts. Enables cluster administrators to monitor messaging infrastructure health.

As a cluster administrator, I want to see metrics for a BrokerService, so that I can monitor performance and capacity.

*Acceptance Criteria:*

- View metrics section with charts: Memory Usage, CPU Usage
- Select time range (1h, 6h, 24h)
- Charts update based on Prometheus queries

*Features:*
- Create reusable MetricsChart component
- Integrate with OpenShift monitoring API
- Time range selector (1h, 6h, 24h)
- Chart rendering
- Loading and error states
- No data state

*Dependencies:* Configure ServiceMonitor

*Acceptance Criteria:*
- Chart component accepts query and renders line chart
- Time range selector updates query and refreshes data
- Loading spinner shows while fetching
